capitals.name: Gudu (camp of the hijra)
capitals.note: The group migrated to Gudu in February 1804. The page gives no coordinates; the point is Sokoto, the nearest gazetteer place, as a proxy.

capitals.name: Sokoto
capitals.note: 'Muhammed Bello... transformed the semi-permanent camp of Sokoto into a city in 1809' (the Sokoto page's infobox gives 1808-1850 and 1851-1902). Infobox also: Birnin Konni 1850, Burmi 1903 in the east; the western co-capital was Gwandu (1808-1811, 1817-1860, 1876-1903), with Bodinga 1811-1817 and Ambursa 1860-1876 (Gwandu page: Abdullahi at Bodinga 1812-1817, Ambursa 1860, Gwandu 1876). [Review af-03-b: held to 1903, not the infobox's 1902, so the capital covers the state's last months: 'On 13 March 1903, at the grand market square of Sokoto, the last Vizier of the Caliphate officially conceded to British Rule' (Sokoto page).]

615k km2 for 1809-1819. The step from 1805 (+136k km2, east to 16.4 E) is the Bornu borderlands (the empire-of-kanem dossier has the same land as a loss in 1809); the rest is the Hausa and Benue lands that no page opened dates. Sokoto is founded as a city in 1809. Infobox area for 1900 is 488,500 km2 against Cliopatria's 792k for 1900 (ratio 0.62, within a factor of two): the Cliopatria outline is the larger and is kept, soft-edged.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1820 shape unchanged, applied for 1820-1823

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria adds 20k km2 on the south-western edge at 1820 (4.0-7.9 E, 8.0-13.3 N). No page opened dates it; the Ilorin page (emirs from 1824) and the Gwandu page (the western territories 'as far west as Dendi' by 1812) are the nearest. Shape kept and holds 1820-1823; Ilorin is added from 1824 below.

New keyframe 1824-1833: the 1820 shape plus Ilorin, which 'became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate under the authority of Gwandu'; the page's list of emirs begins 'Abdusalami dan Salih Alimi 1824-1842' (the alliance of Alimi and Afonja is 'approximately 1810').

793k km2 for 1834-1835. The step (+176k km2, west to 0.2 W, south to 6.5 N, north to 15.2 N) fits the Gwandu page: the polity 'extended as far as Dori' in the west and 'south beyond Ilorin', with Gurma (Dandi, Kamba, Zaberma) and Liptako added 'later' and Ilorin under Gwandu 'by the 1830s'. No page dates the western strips; the step is bridged at 1834 in the ledger.

799k km2 for 1836-1839: the added 7k km2 is the old Oyo core around Oyo-Ile (3.5-4.3 E, 7.6-8.6 N). The Ilorin page: 'Ilorin's forces attacked and burned down Oyo-Ile, the capital of the old Oyo Empire'; no year is given there.
793k km2 for 1840-1894, the 1834 outline again: Oyo-Ile drops out. The Ilorin page: 'Ilorin's southward expansion effectively ended in 1838'. Soft edge throughout.
795k km2 for 1895-1899, 4k km2 of edge noise against 1840 (1.1-16.3 E). Nothing on the pages opened changes in 1895; the French and German advance is undated there.

region.text: Gudu in Gobir, where the community under Usman dan Fodio gathered in February 1804 (the page gives no coordinates; Sokoto is the nearest gazetteer place)

ledger.note: 21 February 1804: the Sokoto jihad begins. Infobox 'Founded: 21 February 1804'; the community under Usman dan Fodio had migrated to Gudu in February 1804, pledged allegiance to him as Commander of the Faithful and appointed flag bearers.

region.text: Gobir, the Rima valley around Alkalawa (the province as a container)

ledger.note: 21 February 1804: 'Yunfa declared war on dan Fodio'. The page dates no battle (Tsuntua, Tabkin Kwatto are undated), so the declaration stands for the first ground held; confidence 1.

1805: the jihadists take Kebbi. 'In 1805' Kebbi was captured; the Gwandu page: Gwandu was established in 1805 after the fall of Birnin Kebbi, and Abdullahi took the Kebbi emirate 'the same year' as Alkalawa (1808).
1807: Katsina and Daura fall. The page has Katsina, Daura and Kano captured in 1807; Katsina's ruler Magajin Halidu killed himself after the defeat (Fulani War).
1807: Kano falls. The page has Katsina, Daura and Kano captured in 1807; King Muhammad Alwali II fled to Zazzau and was killed at Burum-Burum (Fulani War page, which gives Kano no year).

region.text: Nupe, where Mallam Dendo was installed as emir of Bida

ledger.note: c. 1808: Nupe falls. 'The kingdom fell to the Sokoto forces c. 1808' and Mallam Dendo was installed as emir of Bida.

region.text: Ngazargamu and the heart of Bornu

ledger.note: 1808: the jihad reaches Bornu. The jihadists under dan Fodio tried to conquer Borno under Mai Dunama IX Lefiami; they 'burnt the capital, Ngazargamu' and defeated the main army, but only partly succeeded.

region.text: Gobir, the Rima valley around Alkalawa (the province as a container)

ledger.note: 3 October 1808: Alkalawa falls and Gobir with it. 'In 1808, the jihadists assaulted Gobir, killing Yunfa in the battle of Alkalawa' (Sokoto infobox: 'Fall of Alkalawa' 3 October 1808). The Sokoto text says Gobir was 'finally conquered' in 1809.

region.text: Gobir, the Rima valley around Alkalawa (the province as a container)

ledger.note: October 1808: the war with Gobir ends with the fall of Alkalawa.
1809: Bello makes Sokoto a city. 'Muhammed Bello... transformed the semi-permanent camp of Sokoto into a city in 1809'; the infobox gives Sokoto as capital from 1808.

ledger.note: 1809: the Bornu borderlands pass to the caliphate in Cliopatria's shapes. The Sokoto page has only the 1808 attack (it only partly succeeded); the year is the empire-of-kanem dossier's and Cliopatria's step (bridged, page silent).

ledger.note: 1809: Hausaland and the Benue lands complete Cliopatria's outline. The page names the emirates (Zazzau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa and others) without founding years and says the caliphate 'linked over 30 different emirates' at its peak; the year is the Cliopatria step (page silent).

1824: Ilorin is an emirate of the caliphate. 'Ilorin became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate under the authority of Gwandu'; the first emir listed is Abdusalami dan Salih Alimi (1824-1842); Alimi and Afonja allied 'in approximately 1810' against Oyo. The page dates the allegiance to no year, so 1824 is the emirs list.

region.text: Ngazargamu and the heart of Bornu

ledger.note: Later 1820s: the Fulani are driven out of Bornu; the Sokoto page gives no end to the Bornu war (it records Bello's debates with al-Kanemi undated), so 1827 is the empire-of-kanem dossier's bridge.

region.text: the strips added to the 1820 outline: Gurma, Liptako and the lands towards Dori, and the north and south edges

ledger.counterpart: Gurma, Liptako and the lands between (no dossier)
ledger.note: 1834: the western and southern strips complete the caliphate's greatest outline. The Gwandu page: the polity 'extended as far as Dori' and 'south beyond Ilorin'; Gurma and Liptako were added 'later' (no year) and Ilorin was under Gwandu by the 1830s. Year is Cliopatria's step (page silent).

region.text: the old Oyo core around Oyo-Ile

ledger.note: 1836: Ilorin's forces burn Oyo-Ile. 'In a preemptive move, Ilorin's forces attacked and burned down Oyo-Ile, the capital of the old Oyo Empire'; the page gives no year, so 1836 is Cliopatria's step (page silent).

region.text: the old Oyo core around Oyo-Ile

ledger.note: 1840: the old Oyo core drops out of the caliphate's outline. 'Ilorin's southward expansion effectively ended in 1838'; nothing else on the page, so the year is Cliopatria's step (page silent).

region.text: the Nigerian part of the caliphate

ledger.note: 1901: the British move into the caliphate. The page: the British 'by 1901 had begun to move into the Sokoto Caliphate'; the Protectorate page: 'Military operations began in 1902 and continued for about five years of sporadic fighting'.

region.text: the Nigerian part of the caliphate

ledger.note: 13 March 1903: the Vizier concedes. 'On 13 March 1903, at the grand market square of Sokoto, the last Vizier of the Caliphate officially conceded to British Rule'; the Gwandu page: Gwandu capitulated on 12 March 1903.

region.text: the whole caliphate at its end, divided between Britain, France and Germany

ledger.note: [Review af-03-b: confidence 3 to 2, because the page divides the land between the British, French and Germans while this event gives all of it to british-africa.] 1903: the Sokoto Caliphate ends. 'It was dissolved when the British, French, and Germans conquered the area in 1903'; Lugard abolished the caliphate but kept the title of sultan; Attahiru I was beaten in June and the Battle of Burmi is 27 July 1903 (infobox). Cliopatria draws the state to 1904.

wars.outcome: Sokoto victory: Kebbi 1805, Katsina and Kano 1807, Gobir's capital Alkalawa 1808 (Yunfa killed); Sokoto becomes the capital in 1809.
wars.note: The page dates the Tsuntua and Tabkin Kwatto battles to no year; it gives the war as 21 February 1804 to 1808.

wars.name: Sokoto-Bornu war

zones.text: Ngazargamu and the heart of Bornu
the south-western borderlands of Bornu between Cliopatria's 1808 and 1809 shapes, as in the empire-of-kanem dossier

wars.outcome: In 1808 the jihadists burn Ngazargamu but only partly succeeded; Muhammad al-Kanemi leads Bornu's resistance. The south-western borderlands pass to the caliphate in Cliopatria's 1809 shape.
wars.note: The end year 1827 is the empire-of-kanem dossier's; the Sokoto page dates neither the lost borderlands nor the end.

wars.name: Kebbawa resistance (Argungu)
wars.outcome: A combined Sokoto-Gwandu force besieged Argungu in 1831; peace 1831-1849; in 1849 the Kebbawa leader 'renounced his allegiance to the Caliphate and adopted the title of Sarkin Kebbi'; a peace treaty in 1868 ended the hostilities. Argungu is left in the outline: the pages show no change of land.

wars.name: Gobir revolt of 1836
wars.outcome: 'A serious revolt occurred in 1836 in the city-state of Gobir, which was crushed by Muhammed Bello at the Battle of Gawakuke.' No land changed hands.

wars.name: Ilorin-Oyo war

zones.text: the old Oyo core around Oyo-Ile

wars.outcome: Ilorin, an emirate under Gwandu, burns Oyo-Ile and pushes south until 'Ilorin's southward expansion effectively ended in 1838' (the Battle of Osogbo).
wars.note: The page dates only 'the 1830s' (Battle of Ogbomosho) and 1838 (Osogbo); 1830 is the opening of the decade, a bridge.

wars.name: British conquest of the Sokoto Caliphate

zones.text: the Nigerian part of the caliphate

wars.outcome: The British enter in 1901, take Gwandu (12 March) and Sokoto (13 March 1903); Attahiru I is beaten in June and killed; Burmi is 27 July 1903. The French and Germans take their parts (Adamawa to the Germans) in undated moves.
wars.note: The Protectorate page: 'Military operations began in 1902'; 'The remnants of the Bornu Empire were conquered in 1902'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes a Sokoto frontier before the colonial partition; the Hausa heartland is known by emirate, the Sahelian, Benue and Yoruba edges are approximate.

notes: Pages opened: five (budget 5), the Sokoto page three times with different questions. Cliopatria draws its full 479k km2 outline from 1805; the pages date only Kebbi (1805), Katsina, Daura and Kano (1807), Gobir (1808/1809) and Nupe (c. 1808), so 1804-1808 are staged keyframes and the remainder (Zamfara, Zazzau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, the Plateau) enters in one confidence-1 bridge at 1809. The 1834 step (west to Dori, south beyond Ilorin) is from the Gwandu page's extent sentence, undated. The 1820, 1836 and 1840 steps are bridged to Cliopatria. Infobox area 488,500 km2 (1900) against 792k: kept, ratio 0.62. End: 13 March 1903 (Cliopatria 1904). Burmi (27 July 1903) and Attahiru's remnant are in the dissolve note. Not on any page opened: the 1812 or 1815 division into Sokoto and Gwandu is internal (pages disagree: 1812 on the Gwandu page, 1815 on the Sokoto page), the French conquest of Damagaram, Adar and Maradi, the German conquest of Adamawa, Kontagora and Bida, Kano 1903, and the Royal Niger Company treaties; the Sultans' list is not on the page (no rulers strip). Counterparts without dossiers: Sultanate of Gobir, Kingdom of Kebbi (and the Kebbawa of Argungu), Sultanate of Katsina, Sultanate of Kano, Nupe Kingdom, Zamfara, Zazzau, Gurma and Liptako. oyo-empire (af-04) should carry the matching losses of Ilorin (1824) and Oyo-Ile (1836). Gazetteer lacks Gudu, Alkalawa, Gwandu, Oyo-Ile, Dori.
